newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Q1 mortgage delinquencies up at 4.36 pct - MBA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Q1 mortgage delinquencies up at 4.36 pct - MBA.

text.p: U.S. mortgage delinquencies rose in the first quarter of 1997, a second consecutive quarterly increase, according to a survey by the Mortgage Bankers Association of America released Wednesday.

The overall seasonally adjusted delinquency rate on 1-4 unit homes was 4.36 percent in the first quarter, up from 4.32 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996. The Q4 figure was revised down from a previously reported 4.37 percent rate.
The first-quarter rate was 11 basis points below the recent high of 4.47 percent in the first quarter of 1996.

"We expect delinquency rates will continue to hover near or above the current level over the next few quarters, reflecting a growth in consumer debt and the increased number of high loan-to-value ratio loans originated in the past three years," Ron McCord, MBA president, said.
Delinquency rates rose in three of the four regions of the country, the MBA said. The rate in the North Central region fell to 3.88 percent from 3.90 percent in the fourth quarter.
In the West, the rate rose to 3.77 percent, from 3.63 percent. In the Northeast, the rate rose to 4.34 percent, from 4.21 percent. In the South, the rate rose to 5.02 percent, from 4.98 percent.
The delinquency rate increase was concentrated in the 30-day past due category, where delinquencies rose to 3.11 percent from 3.02 percent.
For delinquencies 60 days past due, the rate was unchanged at 0.69 percent, while the rate for 90-day delinquencies fell to a 17-year low to 0.56 percent from 0.61 percent.
Foreclosure rates rose across all loan types in the first quarter, the MBA said. Conventional loans saw a foreclosure rate of 0.72 percent, up from 0.71 percent.
FHA loan foreclosures rose to 1.98 percent from 1.78 percent, while VA loan foreclosures rose to 1.85 percent from 1.62 percent.
MBA for the first time released a breakdown of fixed rate mortgages versus adjustable rate mortgage delinquencies.
Seasonally adjusted delinquency rates on FRM's rose to 3.20 percent from 3.02 percent, while ARM delinquencies rose to 4.45 percent from 4.42 percent.
The MBA survey covers 22 million residential mortgage loans, about one third of all outstanding residential mortgages in the United States, the group said.
